claims.statement: The Commission describes energy performance contracting as a model in which a contractor guarantees expected savings and investment is repaid from those savings.
EU energy-efficiency guidance calls for transparent savings determination and documented measurement, control, and verification independent of participating parties for covered policy measures.

contrary_evidence: Major ESCOs already use established engineering and M&V tools.
The cited independent-verification guidance concerns policy measures and does not itself force every private EPC to use this service.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: a benchmark library of adjustment models, data-quality failures, and dispute outcomes across building types
fingerprint.customer: small ESCOs, energy auditors, lenders, and building owners using performance-based retrofit contracts
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: energy auditors, retrofit lenders, ESCO associations, metering vendors, and municipal renovation programmes
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: neutral data escrow, baseline versioning, weather and occupancy adjustments, uncertainty analysis, and signed calculation packs
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: the contract parties or financing partner pay per monitored site and settlement period
fingerprint.problem_trigger: a monthly settlement closes, a baseline adjustment occurs, or guaranteed savings are disputed

founder_fit: Combines data science, finance, and renewable-energy access; recurring computation is highly automatable and expert review can be channelled through auditors rather than founder-heavy sales.
risks: Baseline model disputes can create liability.
Poor meter or occupancy data undermines results.
Independence must be contractually and operationally credible.

structure.control_point: the mutually accepted, versioned savings calculation that determines a guaranteed-savings payment
structure.critical_dependency: continuous meter and context data plus contractual agreement on baselines, adjustments, independence, and dispute rules

thesis: A neutral measurement-and-verification service can ingest meter, weather, occupancy, intervention, and tariff data, freeze agreed baselines, quantify savings with uncertainty, and produce auditable monthly settlement evidence for energy-performance contracts. Energy auditors, lenders, and ESCO associations distribute it one-to-many; each meter period and contract settlement is recurring.
title: Independent Savings-Settlement Oracle for Small ESCO Portfolios
